problems.title: Fit a square into a right triangle
problems.question: A square shares the right-angle vertex of a triangle with legs 3 and 6 cm; its opposite vertex lies on the hypotenuse. Find its side.
problems.idea: Use similar triangles or the intercept equation of the hypotenuse.
formulas: The hypotenuse through (a,0),(0,b) has equation x/a+y/b=1.
steps: Place the right angle at the origin and the square’s opposite vertex at (s,s).
Then s/3+s/6=1, so s/2=1.
Thus s=2.

problems.title: Bound a simplified radical
problems.question: Find the smallest integer greater than √98-√32.
problems.idea: Extract square factors and compare squares.
steps: Its square is 18, which lies between 4²=16 and 5²=25.
Thus 4<3√2<5, so the required integer is 5.

problems.title: A contact-point segment parallel to the base
problems.question: The incircle divides each equal side of an isosceles triangle into 3 m from the apex and 6 m toward the base. Find the distance between the two contacts on those equal sides.
problems.idea: Equal tangent lengths make the base 12, and the contact segment is a similar-triangle section.
formulas: Equal tangents from a vertex have equal lengths; corresponding lengths in similar triangles have a common ratio.
steps: Each equal side is 9. The two base tangent lengths are 6 each, so the base is 12.
Both contact points are 3/9 of the way from the apex down the equal sides.
Their connecting segment is parallel to the base and has length (3/9)·12=4.

problems.title: A radical domain with a harmless denominator
problems.question: Which listed function has domain [-3,∞)?
problems.idea: The radicand must be nonnegative and the denominator nonzero.
formulas: For √u, require u≥0; |x|+1 is always positive.
steps: For y=√(x+3)/(|x|+1), the square root requires x≥-3.
Its denominator is at least 1, so it excludes no further x.
The endpoint x=-3 is allowed, giving exactly the required domain.

problems.title: The sign of a radical coefficient
problems.question: Solve $(2\sqrt6-5)(3-9x)>0$.
problems.idea: Determine the constant factor’s sign before dividing.
formulas: 2√6=√24<√25=5; dividing an inequality by a negative number reverses it.
steps: The coefficient 2√6-5 is negative.
For the product to be positive, 3-9x must be negative.
Then 9x>3, so x>1/3.
problems.note: The same interval appears twice among the printed choices, so both duplicate options are correct.

problems.title: An angle condition produces similar triangles
problems.question: M lies on AC in triangle ABC, and BAC=MBC. Given AC=8 and BC=6, find MC.
problems.idea: Triangles ABC and BMC have two matching angles.
formulas: In similar triangles, corresponding sides are proportional.
steps: Angle ACB=MCB because M lies on AC; the second equal angle is given.
The correspondence is A↔B, B↔M, C↔C.
Thus MC/BC=BC/AC=6/8.

problems.title: A parallel through the centroid
problems.question: ABC has perimeter 60 cm. A line through its centroid parallel to AC meets AB,BC at M,N, and MN=8 cm. Find the perimeter of trapezoid AMNC.
problems.idea: The centroid lies two thirds of the way from a vertex toward the opposite side.
formulas: The centroid divides each median 2:1 from the vertex; parallel cross-sections give similar triangles.
steps: Triangle BMN is 2/3 the size of ABC. Hence AC=(3/2)MN=12.
The remaining side pieces AM+NC are 1/3 of that sum, or 16.
The trapezoid perimeter is AC+MN+AM+NC=12+8+16=36.

problems.title: Subtract work rates
problems.question: A master finishes a job alone in 6 days and with an apprentice in 4 days. Find the apprentice’s solo time.
problems.idea: The apprentice’s rate is the combined rate minus the master’s.
formulas: Rate=1/completion time.
steps: The apprentice’s daily rate is 1/4-1/6=1/12.
At 1/12 job per day, one full job takes 12 days.

problems.title: Inradii of similar right triangles
problems.question: An altitude to the hypotenuse splits a right triangle into two smaller right triangles. The original inradius is 13 cm and one smaller inradius is 12 cm. Find the other.
problems.idea: All three triangles are similar, so their inradii scale like corresponding hypotenuses.
formulas: If the original legs are a,b and hypotenuse c, the smaller similarity ratios are a/c,b/c; a²+b²=c².
steps: Let the other inradius be r. Similarity gives smaller-to-original ratios 12/13 and r/13.
The squares of these ratios sum to 1 by Pythagoras.
Thus 12²+r²=13², so r²=25 and r=5.

problems.title: Factor the quadratic equation in a system
problems.question: Solve $9x^2-16y^2=0$, $5x+2y=7$.
problems.idea: The first equation splits into two lines.
steps: If 3x=4y, then y=3x/4. Substitute into 5x+2y=7 to get (13/2)x=7, so x=14/13,y=21/26.
If 3x=-4y, then y=-3x/4. Substitution gives (7/2)x=7, so x=2,y=-3/2.
Both pairs satisfy the original quadratic and linear equations.
problems.note: The missing second equation was recovered from the original Word file’s embedded equation.

problems.title: Base lengths from a diagonal ratio
problems.question: A trapezoid has midline 8 cm and its diagonals are divided at their intersection in ratio 1:3. Find the distance between the diagonal midpoints.
problems.idea: The diagonal division ratio equals the base ratio.
formulas: Midline=(a+b)/2; segment joining diagonal midpoints=|b-a|/2.
steps: Write the bases as t and 3t.
Their sum is 16, so 4t=16 and t=4.
The midpoint distance is (12-4)/2=4.

problems.title: Cancel a common radical factor
problems.question: Simplify $(\sqrt{35}-\sqrt{45})/(\sqrt{42}-\sqrt{54})$.
problems.idea: Factor each numerator and denominator using √7-3.
steps: The common factor is nonzero because √7≠3.
After cancellation, the fraction is √5/√6.
Multiply top and bottom by √6 to obtain √30/6.

problems.title: The principal square root is nonnegative
problems.question: For which x is $\sqrt{x^2}=x$ true?
problems.idea: The square root returns the magnitude of x.
steps: If x≥0, |x|=x, so the equality holds.
If x<0, |x|=-x>0 while x<0, so it fails.
Zero is included.

problems.title: Area of a region defined by three inequalities
problems.question: Find the area bounded by y≥-1, x≥1, y≤-0.75x+3.
problems.idea: Find the three line intersections; they form a right triangle.
formulas: Triangle area=perpendicular leg product/2.
steps: At x=1, the upper line gives y=9/4. The vertical leg from -1 to 9/4 has length 13/4.
At y=-1, solve -1=-3x/4+3, giving x=16/3. The horizontal leg from 1 has length 13/3.

problems.title: Congruence needs corresponding data
problems.question: Which listed condition guarantees two triangles are congruent? The final choice specifies a side and its two adjacent angles equal to the corresponding side and adjacent angles of the other triangle.
problems.idea: Angle agreement alone gives similarity; a matching corresponding side fixes the scale.
formulas: ASA congruence: two matching angles and the included corresponding side determine a triangle.
steps: The final choice explicitly matches the side and its adjacent angles, so ASA guarantees congruence.
Three matching angles alone do not fix size: a scaled copy is a counterexample.
Other choices mention angles and sides without explicitly matching their positions. If corresponding positions are assumed, their stronger angle-and-side data also guarantee congruence.
problems.answer: The explicitly corresponding side-and-adjacent-angles condition is unambiguous.
problems.note: Under the usual assumption that all listed equal sides and angles are corresponding, the earlier two-angles-and-a-side and stronger versions are also sufficient. The wording can therefore create multiple correct choices; the final choice is the clearest statement.

problems.title: Similarity scales inradii and hypotenuses
problems.question: Two similar right triangles have inradii differing by 1.5 cm. The larger has perimeter 40 cm and hypotenuse 17 cm. Find the smaller hypotenuse.
problems.idea: Find the larger inradius from its perimeter.
formulas: r=(a+b-c)/2; similar triangles scale all lengths by the same factor.
steps: The larger leg sum is 40-17=23.
Its inradius is (23-17)/2=3. The smaller inradius is 3-1.5=1.5.
The similarity scale is 1.5/3=1/2, so the smaller hypotenuse is 17/2=8.5.

problems.title: Radical terms cancel after expansion
problems.question: Evaluate $(2-\sqrt3)^2+(1+2\sqrt3)^2-(3-\sqrt3)(3+\sqrt3)$.
problems.idea: Expand the two squares and use a difference of squares.
formulas: (u±v)²=u²±2uv+v²; (u-v)(u+v)=u²-v².
steps: The first square is 7-4√3 and the second is 13+4√3.
The last product is 9-3=6.
The total is 7+13-6=14.

problems.title: A rational equation whose quadratic terms cancel
problems.question: Solve $4/(x+2)-1/(x-1)=3/(x+1)$.
problems.idea: State the domain before clearing denominators.
formulas: Exclude x=-2,1,-1; multiply by (x+2)(x-1)(x+1).
steps: Expand: 3x²-3x-6=3x²+3x-6.
Thus 6x=0 and x=0, which is allowed.

problems.title: Three equally spaced trapezoid sections
problems.question: A trapezoid has bases 2 and 10. Three parallel sections divide a leg into four equal parts. Find the sum of their lengths.
problems.idea: The section lengths form an arithmetic progression between the bases.
formulas: At fraction t, length=(1-t)a+tb.
steps: The fractions 1/4,1/2,3/4 give lengths 4,6,8.
Their sum is 4+6+8=18.

problems.title: A system with a recovered lower bound
problems.question: Solve $(2/7)x-1/3<(1/7)x+5/3$, $(x-2)/3\ge(x-6)/6$.
problems.idea: Solve each inequality and keep their overlap.
formulas: A system uses the intersection of solution sets.
steps: The first simplifies to x/7<2, so x<14.
Multiply the second by 6: 2(x-2)≥x-6, giving x≥-2.
Together these give -2≤x<14.
problems.note: The second inequality was recovered from the original Word file’s embedded equation.

problems.title: Locate a radical between integers
problems.question: Which listed unit interval contains $4\sqrt{10}-2$?
problems.idea: Compare 4√10 with 12 and 13 using squares.
formulas: For positive numbers, squaring preserves order.
steps: Subtract 2 to obtain 10<4√10-2<11.

problems.title: Midpoints of medians form a smaller triangle
problems.question: A triangle has perimeter 9.6 m. Find the perimeter of the triangle joining the midpoints of its three medians.
problems.idea: Use coordinates to show that each new side is one quarter of an original side.
formulas: Midpoint of U,V=(U+V)/2 in vector coordinates.
steps: If the original vertices are A,B,C, the midpoint of the median from A is (2A+B+C)/4.
The analogous point from B is (A+2B+C)/4. Their difference is (A-B)/4.
Thus each new side is one quarter of the corresponding original side.
The new perimeter is 9.6/4=2.4.

problems.title: A singular linear system can be inconsistent
problems.question: For which a does x-ay=3, ax-2y=4 have no solution?
problems.idea: Only parallel coefficient rows can prevent a unique intersection.
formulas: Eliminating x gives (a²-2)y=4-3a.
steps: If a²≠2, there is a unique y and therefore a unique solution.
If a=±√2, the coefficient of y is zero.
For either value, 4-3a≠0, so the equation becomes 0=nonzero and is impossible.
problems.note: The second equation ax-2y=4 was recovered from the original Word file’s embedded equation.

problems.title: Chord ratio equals radius ratio at tangency
problems.question: Two circles touch externally. A line through their contact point cuts chords in ratio 3:7. Their centres are 36 cm apart. Find the absolute radius difference.
problems.idea: A homothety centred at the contact point maps one circle to the other.
formulas: Corresponding chord lengths have the same ratio as radii; external centre distance=r+R.
steps: Write r=3t and R=7t.
Their sum is 10t=36, so t=3.6.
The difference is 4t=14.4.

problems.title: Take absolute values before removing square roots
problems.question: Evaluate $\sqrt{(3-2\sqrt3)^2}+\sqrt{(4-2\sqrt3)^2}$.
problems.idea: The two inner expressions have different signs.
steps: The first term is 2√3-3 because 3-2√3<0.
The second is 4-2√3 because 4-2√3>0.
Their sum is 1.
